method: A second ensemble replaces the handcrafted experts by deep ones. A frozen MobileNetV2 [@sandler2018] (width 1.0, publicly released ImageNet weights with 72.2% top-1 accuracy [@li2019mnv2]) embeds three cue-isolating versions of each image: a color layout (the image reduced to 16 × 16 pixels and enlarged again, which removes texture and fine shape), a grayscale high-pass image (the image minus a Gaussian blur of itself with σ = 2 pixels, which removes color and coarse shape) and the binary leaf mask of Section 4.2 (which keeps only the silhouette). Each stream is resized to 224 × 224 pixels, replicated to three channels when needed and normalized with the ImageNet statistics, and the 1,280-dimensional globally pooled embedding is computed once per image. A multinomial logistic-regression head on standardized embeddings is the expert of each stream; the partitions, the V1/V2 protocol and the weight search are those of the handcrafted ensemble (30 re-partitions). A capacity sweep refits each head on the first 16, 64, 256 or 1,280 embedding dimensions (Supplementary S8).
text: **Deep experts.** The deep experts reach 89.00 ± 0.60, 82.95 ± 0.81 and 61.30 ± 0.90% Macro-F1 for the color, texture and shape streams, and their ensemble 92.57 ± 0.58%. Their sharpness differs less than that of the handcrafted experts (0.964, 0.957 and 0.874). The raw weights are consistent with the single-stream ordering in 27/30 partitions and the margin contribution in 30/30 (exact McNemar p = 0.125); with calibrated heads 18/30 and 30/30. Flattening the weakest (shape) stream with its decisions held fixed raises its raw weight from 0.16 to 0.56 while its margin contribution moves from 0.081 to 0.073; the raw weights are then consistent in 5/30 partitions and the margin contribution in 30/30. With experts of similar sharpness the raw weights are mostly usable here, and they fail once the sharpness of one expert is made to depart from the others, as the analysis of Section 3.3 predicts. Across the 64 budget combinations of the sweep (Supplementary S8), the raw weights recover the single-stream ordering in 27% of mixtures, the probability-mass contribution in 89% and the margin contribution in 88%.
supp: Each stream's head was refitted on the first 16, 64, 256 or 1,280 embedding dimensions (a fixed random order) on the fixed partition; mixtures in which two experts lie within one Macro-F1 point would have been excluded, and 64 of the 64 mixtures remained. Recovery of the single-stream ordering by sharpness gap (number of mixtures in brackets): gap 0.00–0.05 [2]: raw 50%, mass 100%, margin 100%; gap 0.05–0.15 [6]: raw 33%, mass 83%, margin 50%; gap 0.15–0.30 [18]: raw 28%, mass 89%, margin 83%; gap 0.30–1.00 [38]: raw 24%, mass 89%, margin 95%. Competence and sharpness vary together in this sweep, so it is descriptive; the effect of sharpness alone is isolated by the flattening experiments.
env: The deep embeddings were computed in the same environment, with the network evaluated in NumPy from the released weights, so no deep-learning framework is needed to reproduce them.
